text.content:
8 September 2047: the wedding, the static, and forty-eight hours of dark.

When: 1–10 September 2047; Static Night itself on 8 September
Where: Night City and every city on the Ziggurat network
Who was involved: A Bartmoss cultist with rogue Biotechnica and Militech allies; Roxanne Lawrence and Luigi Falcone; the cult of Roxanne; a crew led by Fury
What it changed: A second DataKrash was averted, the CitiNet ran clean, NetWatch "reinforced" the Blackwall, and the Purge began in earnest

The Rotten Wire

Ziggurat's CitiNet ran on armored pre-war Old NET trunks it had patched into instead of laying new line, all run from one main server terminal under its Upper Marina headquarters, and linked to the other cities Ziggurat had wired. A rogue Biotechnica cell paid Ziggurat engineers to keep certain trunks "warm" while it fished past the Blackwall for lost research. A rogue Militech cell used the same lines to dig a backdoor into the CitiNet, and made it look like Biotechnica.

The Hijack (1 September)

Every broadcast in Night City was hijacked by a blurred face and a filtered voice that aired every secret of Roxanne Lawrence and Luigi Falcone, heir of the Falcone family. They would marry within one week, he said, or the city would end up like the old Trauma Team tower. Then he fired a rock from a hijacked lunar mass driver, and while the city watched, the old Trauma Team tower in Watson and the block around it were gone. Roxanne became a symbol in minutes, and the wedding the most-watched broadcast in the continent's history.

The Static (8 September)

At the vows the stage blew apart, every screen carrying the broadcast went to static, and the RABIDs rode the signal into the CitiNet. In the same instant came the Flicker: every netrunner jacked into any architecture on the Ziggurat network, in Night City and every city Ziggurat had wired, died at once, brains cooked, decks burned with the same RABID signature. The Council blamed gang netrunners. Out of the smoke a Roxanne rose in a new look to beg for calm, and by noon had a movement; through free prototype Neuroports, something puppeted her fans, and crowds tens of thousands strong set out for Ziggurat HQ to seize the main server terminal.

Forty-Eight Hours

Within an hour the grid failed district by district until the whole city was dark: no power, no CitiNet, no dispatch, no trains. Off the books, a few city leaders paid a crew, coordinated by MaxTac commander Max Hammerman: Fury, Stop Sign, Contender, who joined out of the wreck of the wedding, and Roxanne Lawrence, the real bride, with a MaxTac squad under Stop Sign and Contender. They crossed the city through looting gangs, rogue-cell contractors and puppet crowds they couldn't shoot, and reached Upper Marina on the second night with the cult ten deep around the tower. They went in anyway.

What happened inside is sealed. When the lights came back, the puppets' Neuroports were dead, the RABIDs were gone, and the CitiNet ran clean without the Old NET under it. A week later NetWatch announced it had "reinforced the Blackwall over Night City", with thanks to "local assets". The bomber was later identified as a Rache Bartmoss cultist, working with the rogue cells.

Remembered

Every 8 September at midnight the city unplugs for an hour and Night Corp throttles the CitiNet to emergency traffic. Nobody dives that hour. The Flickerheads wear white noise in memory of the dead.

GM secrets

Lyle Thompson's theories: the Flicker was a mass Soulkiller event whose stolen minds became the bricks of NetWatch's reinforced Blackwall, and the perfect map of where the Old NET touched the world that made the Linkup possible. One member of the crew has a NetWatch connection. Continental Brands was one of the hands that helped end it. And the woman on the stage was a volunteer rebuilt as Roxanne, whose identity no trail has ever reached.

Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.01, 02, 06
